fixes.target: animal-premises-stables:figure-1: The five steps of a fire risk assessment
fixes.value: Flow chart headed "FIRE SAFETY RISK ASSESSMENT" showing five numbered steps in order: 1 Identify fire hazards (sources of ignition, fuel, oxygen); 2 Identify people at risk (people in and around the premises, people especially at risk); 3 Evaluate, remove, reduce and protect from risk (evaluate risk of fire occurring and risk to people, remove or reduce fire hazards and risks to people, with detection and warning, fire-fighting, escape routes, lighting, signs and notices, maintenance). Step 4 is Record, plan, inform, instruct and train (record significant findings and action taken, prepare an emergency plan, inform and instruct relevant people and co-operate and co-ordinate with others, provide training), and step 5 is Review (keep assessment under review, revise where necessary). It ends with the line "Remember to keep to your fire risk assessment under review."
fixes.reason: Image shows the five-step chart with all printed text legible and matching the labels.
fixes.evidence: Five coloured boxes numbered 1 to 5 under a red title bar, red footer reminder.
fixes.by: model check, Claude Code headless Sonnet (packet)

rows: An area through which passes the only escape route from an inner room or area.
A room through which passes the only escape route from an inner room.
A stairway, additional to that required for means of escape purposes, provided for the convenience of occupants.

Guidance issued by government in support of the fire safety aspects of the building regulations.

A means of automatically suppressing, controlling or extinguishing a fire.

A device that is capable of closing the door from any angle and against any latch fitted to the door.

sentences: Glossary of terms: Access area - An area through which passes the only escape route from an inner room or area.
Glossary of terms: Access room - A room through which passes the only escape route from an inner room.
Glossary of terms: Accommodation stairway - A stairway, additional to that required for means of escape purposes, provided for the convenience of occupants.

Glossary of terms: Alternative escape route - Escape routes sufficiently separated by either direction and space, or by fire-resisting construction, to ensure that one is still available irrespective of the location of a fire.
Glossary of terms: Approved Document B (ADB) - Guidance issued by government in support of the fire safety aspects of the building regulations.

Glossary of terms: Automatic fire detection system - A means of automatically detecting the products of a fire and sending a signal to a fire warning system. The design and installation should conform to BS 5839. See ‘Fire warning’.
Glossary of terms: Automatic fire suppression system - A means of automatically suppressing, controlling or extinguishing a fire.

Glossary of terms: Automatic release mechanism - A device that will automatically release either a locking mechanism on an exit route or a hold-open device to a door or roller shutter. It should operate manually, on actuation of the fire warning or detection system or on failure of the power supply.
Glossary of terms: Automatic self-closing device - A device that is capable of closing the door from any angle and against any latch fitted to the door.

Glossary of terms: Basement - A storey with a floor which at some point is more than 1,200mm below the highest level of ground adjacent to the outside walls, unless, and for escape purposes only, such an area has adequate, independent and separate means of escape.
Glossary of terms: Child - A person who is not over compulsory school age, construed in accordance with the Education Act 1996.

Glossary of terms: Class 0 surface spread of flame - Class 0 materials not only restrict the rate of surface spread of flame but also the rate at which heat is released from them. Class 0 is a higher standard than those referred to in British Standards.
Glossary of terms: Compartment wall and/or floor - A fire-resisting wall or floor that separates one fire compartment from another.

Glossary of terms: Competent person - A person with sufficient training and experience or knowledge and other qualities to enable him/her properly to assist in undertaking the preventive and protective measures.

A building, or part of a building, constructed to prevent the spread of fire to or from another part of the same building or an adjoining building.

A fire-resisting enclosure containing a firefighting stair, fire mains, firefighting lobbies and, if provided, a firefighting lift.
sentences: Glossary of terms: Dead end - Area from which escape is possible in one direction only.
Glossary of terms: Direct distance - The shortest distance from any point within the floor area to the nearest storey exit, or fire-resisting route, ignoring walls, partitions and fixings.
Glossary of terms: Domestic premises - Premises occupied as a private dwelling, excluding those areas used in common by the occupants of more than one such dwelling.
Glossary of terms: Emergency lighting - Lighting provided for use when the supply to the normal lighting fails.
Glossary of terms: Enforcing authority - The fire and rescue authority or any other authority specified in Article 25 of the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005.
Glossary of terms: Escape lighting - That part of the lighting system provided to enable people to use the escape route (it may be the normal lighting system).
Glossary of terms: Escape route - Route forming that part of the means of escape from any point in a building to a final exit.
Glossary of terms: Evacuation lift - A lift that may be used for the evacuation of people with disabilities, or others, in a fire.
Glossary of terms: External escape stair - Stair providing an escape route, external to the building.
Glossary of terms: False alarm - A fire signal, usually from a fire warning system, resulting from a cause other than fire.
Glossary of terms: Final exit - An exit from a building where people can continue to disperse in safety and where they are no longer in danger from fire and/or smoke.
Glossary of terms: Fire compartment - A building, or part of a building, constructed to prevent the spread of fire to or from another part of the same building or an adjoining building.

Glossary of terms: Firefighting shaft - A fire-resisting enclosure containing a firefighting stair, fire mains, firefighting lobbies and, if provided, a firefighting lift.

rows: Place of total safety for animals
An emergency enclosure, preferably upwind from the fire, where animals can be taken and are at no immediate danger from the effects of a fire.
Any place, such as a building and the immediate land bounded by any enclosure of it, any tent, moveable or temporary structure or any installation or workplace.
An escape strategy that allows for the horizontal movement of people, from one fire compartment to another, away from the fire.
A fire-resisting enclosure providing access to an escape stairway via two sets of fire-resisting doors and into which no room opens other than toilets and lifts.
A stairway which is adequately protected from the rest of the building by fire-resisting construction.

A place within a building or structure where, for a limited period of time, people will have some protection from the effects of fire and smoke. This place, usually a corridor or stairway, will normally have a minimum of 30 minutes fire resistance and allow people to continue their escape to a place of total safety.
An area of reasonable safety in which a disabled person may rest prior to reaching a place of total safety. It should lead directly to a fire-resisting escape route.
The person ultimately responsible for fire safety as defined in the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005.

A feature of the premises, its contents or occupants that may have an adverse effect on the means of escape in case of fire, resulting in a potential risk to people within or in the vicinity of the premises.
A system of evacuation in which all people evacuate immediately on hearing the fire warning.
Device containing within one housing all the components, except possibly the energy source, for detecting smoke and giving an audible alarm.
A fire warning system which can produce a number of staged alarms within a given area.
An exit giving direct access into a fire-resisting stairway or an external escape route.
The actual distance to be travelled by a person from any point within the floor area to the nearest storey exit or final exit, having regard to the layout of walls, partitions and fixings.
A transparent panel in a wall or door of an inner room enabling the occupant to become aware of a fire in the access area during the early stages.
sentences: Glossary of terms: Place of total safety for animals is defined as an emergency enclosure, preferably upwind from the fire, where animals can be taken and are at no immediate danger from the effects of a fire.

Glossary of terms: Premises is defined as any place, such as a building and the immediate land bounded by any enclosure of it, any tent, moveable or temporary structure or any installation or workplace.
Glossary of terms: Progressive horizontal evacuation is defined as an escape strategy that allows for the horizontal movement of people, from one fire compartment to another, away from the fire.

Glossary of terms: Protected lobby is defined as a fire-resisting enclosure providing access to an escape stairway via two sets of fire-resisting doors and into which no room opens other than toilets and lifts.
Glossary of terms: Protected stairway is defined as a stairway which is adequately protected from the rest of the building by fire-resisting construction.

Glossary of terms: Reasonable safety is defined as a place within a building or structure where, for a limited period of time, people will have some protection from the effects of fire and smoke; this place, usually a corridor or stairway, will normally have a minimum of 30 minutes fire resistance and allow people to continue their escape to a place of total safety.

Glossary of terms: Refuge is defined as an area of reasonable safety in which a disabled person may rest prior to reaching a place of total safety; it should lead directly to a fire-resisting escape route.
Glossary of terms: Responsible person is defined as the person ultimately responsible for fire safety as defined in the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005.

Glossary of terms: Significant finding is defined as a feature of the premises, its contents or occupants that may have an adverse effect on the means of escape in case of fire, resulting in a potential risk to people within or in the vicinity of the premises.
Glossary of terms: Simultaneous evacuation is defined as a system of evacuation in which all people evacuate immediately on hearing the fire warning.
Glossary of terms: Smoke alarm is defined as a device containing within one housing all the components, except possibly the energy source, for detecting smoke and giving an audible alarm.
Glossary of terms: Staged alarm is defined as a fire warning system which can produce a number of staged alarms within a given area.
Glossary of terms: Storey exit is defined as an exit giving direct access into a fire-resisting stairway or an external escape route.

Glossary of terms: Travel distance is defined as the actual distance to be travelled by a person from any point within the floor area to the nearest storey exit or final exit, having regard to the layout of walls, partitions and fixings.
Glossary of terms: Vision panel is defined as a transparent panel in a wall or door of an inner room enabling the occupant to become aware of a fire in the access area during the early stages.

The Order requires that fire precautions (such as firefighting equipment, fire detection and warning, and emergency routes and exits) should be provided (and maintained) ‘where necessary’. What this means is that the fire precautions you must provide (and maintain) are those which are needed to reasonably protect relevant persons from risks to them in case of fire. This will be determined by the findings of your risk assessment including the preventative measures you have or will have taken. In practice, it is very unlikely, that a properly conducted fire risk assessment, which takes into account all the matters relevant for the safety of persons in case of fire, will conclude that no fire precautions (including maintenance) are necessary.

The Glossary defines Alterations notice as: If your premises are considered by the enforcing authority to be high-risk, they may issue an alterations notice that requires you to inform them before making any material alterations to your premises.

The Glossary defines Alternative escape route as: Escape routes sufficiently separated by either direction and space, or by fire-resisting construction to ensure that one is still available irrespective of the location of a fire.
The Glossary defines Approved Document B (ADB)²⁴ as: Guidance issued by Government in support of the fire safety aspects of the building regulations.

rows: A Hospital Street is a special type of compartment which connects final exits, stairway enclosures and department entrances and serves as a firefighting bridgehead and a safe evacuation route for occupants to parts of the building unaffected by fire.
A room from which escape is possible only by passing through another room (the access room).
Any premises that require a licence under any statute to undertake trade or conduct business activities.
An alteration to a building, process or service which significantly affects the level of risk to people from a fire in those premises.
Route(s) provided to ensure safe egress from premises or other locations to a place of total safety.
A system of evacuation in which different parts of the premises are evacuated in a controlled sequence of phases, those parts of the premises expected to be at greatest risk being evacuated first.

A place within a building or structure where, for a limited period of time, people will have some protection from the effects of fire and smoke. This place, usually a corridor, protected area or protected stairway, will normally have a minimum of 30 minutes’ fire resistance and allow people to continue their escape to a place of total safety.
A place, away from the premises, in which people are at no immediate danger from the effects of a fire.
Any place, such as a building and the immediate land bounded by any enclosure of it, any tent, moveable or temporary structure or any installation or workplace.
An escape strategy that allows for the horizontal movement of people, from one fire compartment (protected area) to another, away from the fire.
A fire-resisting enclosure providing access to an escape stairway via two sets of fire doors and into which no room opens other than toilets and lifts.
A stairway which is adequately protected from the rest of the building by fire-resisting construction.
An escape route which is adequately protected from the rest of the building by fire-resisting construction.

A place of reasonable safety in which a disabled person or others who may need assistance may rest or wait for assistance before reaching a place of total safety. It should lead directly to a fire- resisting escape route.
Any person lawfully on the premises and any person in the immediate vicinity, but does not include firefighters carrying out firefighting duties.

rows: The Order¹ requires that fire precautions (such as firefighting equipment, fire detection and warning, and emergency routes and exits) should be provided (and maintained) ‘where necessary’. What this means is that the fire precautions you must provide (and maintain) are those which are needed to reasonably protect relevant people from risks to them in case of fire. This will be determined by the finding of your risk assessment, including the preventative measures you have or will have taken. In practice, it is very unlikely that a properly conducted fire risk assessment, which takes into account all the matters relevant for the safety of people in case of fire, will conclude that no fire precautions (including maintenance) are necessary.

a. A person aged 16 years, from the date on which he attains that age until and including the 31st August which next follows that date. b. A person aged 16 years and over who is undertaking a course of full-time education at a school or college which is not advanced education. c. A person aged 16 years and over who is undertaking approved training that is not provided through a contract of employment. For the purpose of pargraphs (b) and (c) the person: a. shall have commenced the course of full-time education or approved training before attaining the age of 19 years; and b. shall not have attained the age of 20 years.

Glossary: the term 'Young person' means a. a person aged 16 years, from the date on which he attains that age until and including the 31st August which next follows that date; b. a person aged 16 years and over who is undertaking a course of full-time education at a school or college which is not advanced education; c. a person aged 16 years and over who is undertaking approved training that is not provided through a contract of employment; for the purpose of pargraphs (b) and (c) the person a. shall have commenced the course of full-time education or approved training before attaining the age of 19 years; and b. shall not have attained the age of 20 years.

Guidance issued by Government in support of the fire safety aspects of the building regulations.
Is a concept where risks should continue to be reduced until you reach a point where the cost and effort to reduce the risk further would be grossly disproportionate to the benefit achieved.

sentences: The Glossary defines Access room as a room through which the only escape route from an inner room passes.
The Glossary defines Accommodation stairway as a stairway, additional to that required for means of escape purposes provided for the convenience of occupants.

The Glossary defines Alterations notice as follows: if your premises are considered by the enforcing authority to be high risk, they may issue an alterations notice that requires you to inform them before making any material alterations to your premises.

The Glossary defines Alternative escape route as escape routes sufficiently separated by either direction and space, or by fire-resisting construction to ensure that one is still available irrespective of the location of a fire.
The Glossary defines Approved Document B (ADB) as guidance issued by Government in support of the fire safety aspects of the building regulations.

The Glossary defines As low as reasonably practicable as a concept where risks should continue to be reduced until you reach a point where the cost and effort to reduce the risk further would be grossly disproportionate to the benefit achieved.
The Glossary defines Automatic fire detection system as a means of automatically detecting the products of a fire and sending a signal to a fire warning system, and says to see ‘Fire warning’.

The Glossary defines Basement as a storey with a floor which at some point is more than 1,200mm below the highest level of ground adjacent to the outside walls, unless, and for escape purposes only, such area has adequate, independent and separate means of escape.
The Glossary defines Child as anyone who is not over compulsory school age, i.e. before or just after their 16th birthday.

The Glossary defines Class 0, 1 or 3 surface spread of flame as classes of surface spread of flame for materials needed to line the walls and ceilings of escape routes, and says to see Appendix B for further information.
The Glossary defines Combustible material as a substance that can be burned.
The Glossary defines Compartment wall and/or floor as a fire-resisting wall or floor that separates one fire compartment from another.

The Glossary defines Competent person as a person with enough training and experience or knowledge and other qualities to enable them properly to assist in undertaking the preventive and protective measures.

Area from which escape is possible in one direction only.
The shortest distance from any point within the floor area to the nearest storey exit, or fire-resisting route, ignoring walls, partitions and fixings.
Premises occupied as a private dwelling, excluding those areas used in common by the occupants of more than one such dwelling.

The fire and rescue authority or any other authority specified in Article 25 of the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005.¹

A fire signal, usually from a fire warning system, resulting from a cause other than fire.

A building, or part of a building, constructed to prevent the spread of fire to or from another part of the same building or an adjoining building.

sentences: The Glossary defines Dangerous substance as: 1. A substance which because of its physico-chemical or chemical properties and the way it is used or is present at the workplace creates a risk. 2. A substance subject to the Dangerous Substances and Explosive Atmosphere Regulations 2002 (DSEAR).
The Glossary defines Dead end as an area from which escape is possible in one direction only.
The Glossary defines Direct distance as the shortest distance from any point within the floor area to the nearest storey exit, or fire-resisting route, ignoring walls, partitions and fixings.
The Glossary defines Domestic premises as premises occupied as a private dwelling, excluding those areas used in common by the occupants of more than one such dwelling.
The Glossary defines Emergency escape lighting as lighting provided to illuminate escape routes that will function if the normal lighting fails.
The Glossary defines Enforcing authority as the fire and rescue authority or any other authority specified in Article 25 of the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005.
The Glossary defines Escape route as the route forming that part of the means of escape from any point in the premises to a final exit.
The Glossary defines Evacuation lift as a lift that may be used for the evacuation of people with disabilities, or others, in a fire.
The Glossary defines External escape stair as a stair providing an escape route, external to the building.

The Glossary defines Fail-safe as locking an output device with the application of power and having the device unlock when the power is removed, also known as fail unlock, reverse action or power locked.
The Glossary defines False alarm as a fire signal, usually from a fire warning system, resulting from a cause other than fire.
The Glossary defines Final exit as an exit from a building where people can continue to disperse in safety and where they are no longer at danger from fire and/or smoke.
The Glossary defines Fire compartment as a building, or part of a building, constructed to prevent the spread of fire to or from another part of the same building or an adjoining building.

The Glossary defines Fire door as a door or shutter, together with its frame and furniture, provided for the passage of people, air or goods which, when closed is intended to restrict the passage of fire and/or smoke to a predictable level of performance.

The Glossary defines Firefighting lift as a lift, designed to have additional protection, with controls that enable it to be used under the direct control of the fire and rescue service when fighting a fire.
The Glossary defines Firefighting shaft as a fire-resisting enclosure containing a firefighting stair, fire mains, firefighting lobbies and if provided, a firefighting lift.

rows: The ability of a component or construction of a building to satisfy, for a stated period of time, some or all of the appropriate criteria of relevant standards. (Generally described as 30 minutes fire-resisting or 60 minutes fire-resisting.) See BS EN 1363-1,⁴⁶ BS 476-7³³ and associated standards for further information.
A nominated person with responsibility for carrying out day-to-day management of fire safety. (This may or may not be the same as the ‘responsible person’.)
A number of planned and co-ordinated arrangements designed to reduce the risk of fire and to ensure the safety of people if there is a fire.
A seal provided to close an imperfection of fit or design tolerance between elements or components, to restrict the passage of fire and smoke.
A means of alerting people to the existence of a fire. (See automatic fire detection system.)
Easily ignited and capable of burning rapidly.
Generally liquids with a flashpoint of below 21°C. (The Chemicals Hazard Information and Packaging for Supply Regulations 2002⁴⁷ (CHIP) give more detailed guidance.)
1. See Dangerous substance. 2. A substance subject to the Control of Substances Hazardous to Health Regulations 2002 (COSHH).
A room from which escape is possible only by passing through another room (the access room).
Any premises that require a licence under any statute to undertake trade or conduct business activities.
An alteration to the premises, process or service which significantly affects the level of risk to people from fire in those premises.
Route(s) provided to ensure safe egress from the premises or other locations to a place of total safety.
A system of evacuation in which different parts of the premises are evacuated in a controlled sequence of phases, those parts of the premises expected to be at greatest risk being evacuated first.

A place within a building or structure where, for a limited period of time, people will have some protection from the effects of fire and smoke. This place, usually a corridor or stairway, will normally have a minimum of 30 minutes fire resistance and allow people to continue their escape to a place of total safety.

The Glossary defines Fire safety manager as a nominated person with responsibility for carrying out day-to-day management of fire safety, who may or may not be the same as the ‘responsible person’.
The Glossary defines Fire safety strategy as a number of planned and co-ordinated arrangements designed to reduce the risk of fire and to ensure the safety of people if there is a fire.
The Glossary defines Fire stopping as a seal provided to close an imperfection of fit or design tolerance between elements or components, to restrict the passage of fire and smoke.

The Order requires that fire precautions (such as firefighting equipment, fire detection and warning, and emergency routes and exits) should be provided (and maintained) ‘where necessary’. What this means is that the fire precautions you must provide (and maintain) are those which are needed to reasonably protect relevant persons from risks to them in case of fire. This will be determined by the findings of your risk assessment including the preventative measures you have or will have taken. In practice, it is very unlikely, that a properly conducted fire risk assessment, which takes into account all the matters relevant for the safety of persons in case of fire, will conclude that no fire precautions (including maintenance) are necessary.

rows: A room through which the only escape route from an inner room passes.
A stairway, additional to that required for means of escape purposes, provided for the convenience of occupants.

If your premises are considered by the enforcing authority to be high risk, they may issue an alterations notice that requires you to inform them before making any material alterations to your premises.
Escape routes sufficiently separated by either direction and space, or by fire-resisting construction to ensure that one is still available irrespective of the location of a fire.
Guidance issued by Government in support of the fire safety aspects of the building regulations.
Is a concept where risks should continue to be reduced until you reach a point where the cost and effort to reduce the risk further would be grossly disproportionate to the benefit achieved.
A means of automatically detecting the products of a fire and sending a signal to a fire warning system. See ‘Fire warning’.

A storey with a floor which at some point is more than 1,200mm below the highest level of ground adjacent to the outside walls, unless, and for escape purposes only, such area has adequate, independent and separate means of escape.
Anyone who is not over compulsory school age, i.e. before or just after their 16th birthday.
Class 0, 1 or 3 surface spread of flame
Classes of surface spread of flame for materials needed to line the walls and ceilings of escape routes. See Appendix B for further information.
A substance that can be burned.

sentences: In the Glossary, Access room is defined as: A room through which the only escape route from an inner room passes.
In the Glossary, Accommodation stairway is defined as: A stairway, additional to that required for means of escape purposes, provided for the convenience of occupants.

In the Glossary, Alterations notice is defined as: If your premises are considered by the enforcing authority to be high risk, they may issue an alterations notice that requires you to inform them before making any material alterations to your premises.

In the Glossary, Alternative escape route is defined as: Escape routes sufficiently separated by either direction and space, or by fire-resisting construction to ensure that one is still available irrespective of the location of a fire.
In the Glossary, Approved Document B (ADB)²⁴ is defined as: Guidance issued by Government in support of the fire safety aspects of the building regulations.

In the Glossary, As low as reasonably practicable is defined as: Is a concept where risks should continue to be reduced until you reach a point where the cost and effort to reduce the risk further would be grossly disproportionate to the benefit achieved.
In the Glossary, Automatic fire detection system is defined as: A means of automatically detecting the products of a fire and sending a signal to a fire warning system. See ‘Fire warning’.

In the Glossary, Basement is defined as: A storey with a floor which at some point is more than 1,200mm below the highest level of ground adjacent to the outside walls, unless, and for escape purposes only, such area has adequate, independent and separate means of escape.
In the Glossary, Child is defined as: Anyone who is not over compulsory school age, i.e. before or just after their 16th birthday.

In the Glossary, Class 0, 1 or 3 surface spread of flame is defined as: Classes of surface spread of flame for materials needed to line the walls and ceilings of escape routes. See Appendix B for further information.
In the Glossary, Combustible material is defined as: A substance that can be burned.
In the Glossary, Compartment wall and/or floor is defined as: A fire-resisting wall or floor that separates one fire compartment from another.

In the Glossary, External escape stair is defined as: Stair providing an escape route, external to the building.

The Order requires that fire precautions (such as firefighting equipment, fire detection and warning, and emergency routes and exits) should be provided (and maintained) ‘where necessary’. What this means is that the fire precautions you must provide (and maintain) are those which are needed to reasonably protect relevant persons from risks to them in case of fire. This will be determined by the findings of your risk assessment including the preventative measures you have or will have taken. In practice, it is very unlikely, that a properly conducted fire risk assessment, which takes into account all the matters relevant for the safety of persons in case of fire, will conclude that no fire precautions (including maintenance) are necessary.

(a) A person aged 16 years, from the date on which he attains that age until and including the 31st August which next follows that date. (b) A person aged 16 years and over who is undertaking a course of full-time education at a school or college which is not advanced education. (c) A person aged 16 years and over who is undertaking approved training that is not provided through a contract of employment. For the purposes of paragraphs (b) and (c) the person: (a) shall have commenced the course of full-time education or approved training before attaining the age of 19 years; and (b) shall not have attained the age of 20 years.

fixes.target: open-air-events-venues:figure-1: The five steps of a fire risk assessment
fixes.value: A flow chart titled FIRE SAFETY RISK ASSESSMENT with five numbered steps in coloured boxes. Step 1 Identify fire hazards (sources of ignition, fuel and oxygen); Step 2 Identify people at risk (people in and around the premises, people especially at risk); Step 3 Evaluate, remove, reduce and protect from risk (evaluate the risk of a fire occurring and the risk to people from fire, remove or reduce fire hazards and the risks to people, with bullets Detection and warning, Fire-fighting, Escape routes, Lighting, Signs and notices, Maintenance). Step 4 is Record, plan, inform, instruct and train (record significant finding and action taken, prepare an emergency plan, inform and instruct relevant people; co-operate and co-ordinate with others, provide training); Step 5 is Review (keep assessment under review, revise where necessary), and a bottom banner reads: Remember to keep to your fire risk assessment under review.

rows: An alteration to a building, process or service which significantly affects the level of risk in that building.
Route(s) provided to ensure safe egress from a site, event or venue or other locations to a place of total safety.

A system of evacuation in which different parts of the site, event or venue are evacuated in a controlled sequence of phases, those parts of the site, event or venue expected to be at greatest risk being evacuated first.

A place within a site, event or venue where, for a limited period of time, people will have some protection from the effects of fire and smoke. This place must allow people to continue their escape to a place of total safety.
A place, away from the site, event or venue, in which people are at no immediate danger from the effects of a fire.
Any place (including the open air), such as a building and the immediate land bounded by any enclosure of it, any tent, moveable or temporary structure or any installation or workplace.
An area of reasonable safety in which a disabled person may rest before reaching a place of total safety. It should lead directly to a fire-resisting escape route.
The person ultimately responsible for fire safety as defined in the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005.

A feature of the site, event or venue, from which the fire hazards and persons at risk are identified. The actions you have taken or will take to remove or reduce the chance of a fire occurring or the spread of fire and smoke. The actions people need to take in case of fire. The necessary information, instruction and training needed and how it will be given.
Device containing within one housing all the components, except possibly the energy source, for detecting smoke and giving an audible alarm.
A fire warning which can be given in two or more stages for different purposes within a given area (i.e. notifying staff, stand by to evacuate, full evacuation).
The actual distance to be travelled by a person from any point within the floor area to the nearest storey exit or final exit, having regard to the layout of wall, partitions and fixings.
sentences: In the Glossary, Material change means: An alteration to a building, process or service which significantly affects the level of risk in that building.
In the Glossary, Means of escape means: Route(s) provided to ensure safe egress from a site, event or venue or other locations to a place of total safety.

In the Glossary, Phased evacuation means: A system of evacuation in which different parts of the site, event or venue are evacuated in a controlled sequence of phases, those parts of the site, event or venue expected to be at greatest risk being evacuated first.

In the Glossary, Place of reasonable safety means: A place within a site, event or venue where, for a limited period of time, people will have some protection from the effects of fire and smoke. This place must allow people to continue their escape to a place of total safety.
In the Glossary, Place of total safety means: A place, away from the site, event or venue, in which people are at no immediate danger from the effects of a fire.

In the Glossary, Premises means: Any place (including the open air), such as a building and the immediate land bounded by any enclosure of it, any tent, moveable or temporary structure or any installation or workplace.
In the Glossary, Refuge means: An area of reasonable safety in which a disabled person may rest before reaching a place of total safety. It should lead directly to a fire-resisting escape route.
In the Glossary, Responsible person means: The person ultimately responsible for fire safety as defined in the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005.

In the Glossary, Significant finding means: A feature of the site, event or venue, from which the fire hazards and persons at risk are identified. The actions you have taken or will take to remove or reduce the chance of a fire occurring or the spread of fire and smoke. The actions people need to take in case of fire. The necessary information, instruction and training needed and how it will be given.
In the Glossary, Smoke alarm means: Device containing within one housing all the components, except possibly the energy source, for detecting smoke and giving an audible alarm.

In the Glossary, Staged fire alarms means: A fire warning which can be given in two or more stages for different purposes within a given area (i.e. notifying staff, stand by to evacuate, full evacuation).

In the Glossary, Travel distance means: The actual distance to be travelled by a person from any point within the floor area to the nearest storey exit or final exit, having regard to the layout of wall, partitions and fixings.

rows: The Order requires that fire precautions (such as firefighting equipment, fire detection and warning, and emergency routes and exits) should be provided (and maintained) ‘where necessary’. What this means is that the fire precautions you must provide (and maintain) are those which are needed to reasonably protect relevant person from risks to them in case of fire. This will be determined by the finding of your risk assessment including the preventative measures you have or will have taken. In practice, it is very unlikely, that a properly conducted fire risk assessment, which takes into account all the matters relevant for the safety of persons in case of fire, will conclude that no fire precautions (including maintenance) are necessary.

(a) A person aged 16 years, from the date on which he attains that age until and including the 31st August which next follows that date. (b) A person aged 16 years and over who is undertaking a course of full-time education at a school or college which is not advanced education. (c) A person aged 16 years and over who is undertaking approved training that is not provided through a contract of employment. For the purposes of paragraphs (b) and (c) the person: (a) shall have commenced the course of full-time education or approved training before attaining the age of 19 years: and (b) shall not have attained the age of 20 years.

sentences: Glossary: Access room means a room through which the only escape route from an inner room passes.
Glossary: Accommodation stairway means a stair, additional to that required for means of escape purposes, provided for the convenience of occupants.

Glossary: Alterations notice means if your premises are considered by the enforcing authority to be high risk, they may issue an alterations notice that requires you to inform them before making any material alterations to your premises.

Glossary: Alternative escape route means escape routes sufficiently separated by either direction and space, or by fire-resisting construction to ensure that one is still available irrespective of the location of a fire.
Glossary: Approved Document B (ADB)24 means guidance issued by Government in support of the fire safety aspects of the building regulations.

Glossary: As low as reasonably practicable is a concept where risks should continue to be reduced until you reach a point where the cost and effort to reduce the risk further would be grossly disproportionate to the benefit achieved.
Glossary: Automatic fire-detection system means a means of automatically detecting the products of a fire and sending a signal to a fire warning system. See ‘Fire warning’.

Glossary: Basement means a storey with a floor which at some point is more than 1,200mm below the highest level of ground adjacent to the outside walls, unless, and for escape purposes only, such area has adequate, independent and separate means of escape.
Glossary: Child means anyone who is not over compulsory school age, i.e. before or just after their 16th birthday.

Glossary: Class 0, 1 or 3 surface spread of flame means classes of surface spread of flame for materials needed to line the walls and ceilings of escape routes. See Appendix B for further information.
Glossary: Combustible material means a substance that can be burned.
Glossary: Compartment wall and/or floor means a fire-resisting wall or floor that separates one fire compartment from another.
Glossary: Competent person means a person with enough training and experience or knowledge and other qualities to enable them properly to assist in undertaking the preventive and protective measures.

rows: Low mounted luminous tracks positioned on escape routes in combination with exit indicators, exit marking and intermediate direction indicators along the route, provided for use when the supply to the normal lighting fails, which do not rely on an electrical supply for their luminous output.

The Order requires that fire precautions (such as firefighting equipment, fire detection and warning, and emergency routes and exits) should be provided (and maintained) ‘where necessary’. What this means is that the fire precautions you must provide (and maintain) are those which are needed to reasonably protect relevant persons from risks to them in case of fire. This will be determined by the findings of your risk assessment including the preventative measures you have or will have taken. In practice, it is very unlikely, that a properly conducted fire risk assessment, which takes into account all the matters relevant for the safety of persons in case of fire, will conclude that no fire precautions (including maintenance) are necessary.

(a) A person aged 16 years, from the date on which he attains that age until and including the 31st August which next follows that date. (b) A person aged 16 years and over who is undertaking a course of full-time education at a school or college which is not advanced education. (c) A person aged 16 years and over who is undertaking approved training that is not provided through a contract of employment. For the purposes of paragraphs (b) and (c) the person: (a) shall have commenced the course of full-time education or approved training before attaining the age of 19 years; and (b) shall not have attained the age of 20 years.

sentences: Glossary. Access room: A room through which the only escape route from an inner room passes.
Glossary. Accommodation stairway: A stair, additional to that required for means of escape purposes, provided for the convenience of occupants.

Glossary. Alterations notice: If your premises are considered by the enforcing authority to be high risk, they may issue an alterations notice that requires you to inform them before making any material alterations to your premises.

Glossary. Alternative escape route: Escape routes sufficiently separated by either direction and space, or by fire-resisting construction to ensure that one is still available irrespective of the location of a fire.
Glossary. Approved Document B (ADB)²⁴: Guidance issued by Government in support of the fire safety aspects of the building regulations.

Glossary. As low as reasonably practicable: Is a concept where risks should continue to be reduced until you reach a point where the cost and effort to reduce the risk further would be grossly disproportionate to the benefit achieved.
Glossary. Automatic fire-detection system: A means of automatically detecting the products of a fire and sending a signal to a fire warning system. See ‘Fire warning’.

Glossary. Basement: A storey with a floor which at some point is more than 1,200mm below the highest level of ground adjacent to the outside walls, unless, and for escape purposes only, such area has adequate, independent and s eparate means of escape.
Glossary. Child: Anyone who is not over compulsory school age, i.e. before or just after their 16th birthday.
Glossary. Class 0, 1 or 3 surface spread of flame: Classes of surface spread of flame for materials needed to line the walls and ceilings of escape routes. See Appendix B for further information.
Glossary. Combustible material: A substance that can be burned.
Glossary. Compartment wall and/or floor: A fire-resisting wall or floor that separates one fire compartment from another.
Glossary. Competent person: A person with enough training and experience or knowledge and other qualities to enable them properly to assist in undertaking the preventive and protective measures.

A final exit or a doorway giving direct access into a protected stairway, firefighting lobby or external escape route.
The actual distance to be travelled by a person from any point within the floor area to the nearest storey exit or final exit, having regard to the layout of walls, partitions and fixings.
A transparent panel in a wall or door of an inner room enabling the occupant to become aware of a fire in the access area during the early stages.

Low mounted luminous tracks positioned on escape routes in combination with exit indicators, exit marking and intermediate direction indicators along the route, provided for use when the supply to the normal lighting fails, which do not rely on an electrical supply for their luminous output.

The Order requires that fire precautions (such as firefighting equipment, fire detection and warning, and emergency routes and exits) should be provided (and maintained) ‘where necessary’. What this means is that the fire precautions you must provide (and maintain) are those which are needed to reasonably protect relevant persons from risks to them in case of fire. This will be determined by the findings of your risk assessment including the preventative measures you have or will have taken. In practice, it is very unlikely, that a properly conducted fire risk assessment, which takes into account all the matters relevant for the safety of persons in case of fire, will conclude that no fire precautions (including maintenance) are necessary.

(a) A person aged 16 years, from the date on which he attains that age until and including the 31st August which next follows that date. (b) A person aged 16 years and over who is undertaking a course of full-time education at a school or college which is not advanced education. (c) A person aged 16 years and over who is undertaking approved training that is not provided through a contract of employment. For the purposes of paragraphs (b) and (c) the person: (a) shall have commenced the course of full-time education or approved training before attaining the age of 19 years; and (b) shall not have attained the age of 20 years.

Glossary. Storey exit: A final exit or a doorway giving direct access into a protected stairway, firefighting lobby or external escape route.

Glossary. Travel distance: The actual distance to be travelled by a person from any point within the floor area to the nearest storey exit or final exit, having regard to the layout of walls, partitions and fixings.
Glossary. Vision panel: A transparent panel in a wall or door of an inner room enabling the occupant to become aware of a fire in the access area during the early stages.

Glossary. Way guidance: Low mounted luminous tracks positioned on escape routes in combination with exit indicators, exit marking and intermediate direction indicators along the route, provided for use when the supply to the normal lighting fails, which do not rely on an electrical supply for their luminous output.

Glossary. Where necessary: The Order requires that fire precautions (such as firefighting equipment, fire detection and warning, and emergency routes and exits) should be provided (and maintained) ‘where necessary’. What this means is that the fire precautions you must provide (and maintain) are those which are needed to reasonably protect relevant persons from risks to them in case of fire. This will be determined by the findings of your risk assessment including the preventative measures you have or will have taken. In practice, it is very unlikely, that a properly conducted fire risk assessment, which takes into account all the matters relevant for the safety of persons in case of fire, will conclude that no fire precautions (including maintenance) are necessary.

Glossary. Young person: (a) A person aged 16 years, from the date on which he attains that age until and including the 31st August which next follows that date. (b) A person aged 16 years and over who is undertaking a course of full-time education at a school or college which is not advanced education. (c) A person aged 16 years and over who is undertaking approved training that is not provided through a contract of employment. For the purposes of paragraphs (b) and (c) the person: (a) shall have commenced the course of full-time education or approved training before attaining the age of 19 years; and (b) shall not have attained the age of 20 years.

The Order requires that fire precautions (such as firefighting equipment, fire detection and warning, and emergency routes and exits) should be provided (and maintained) ‘where necessary’. What this means is that the fire precautions you must provide (and maintain) are those which are needed to reasonably protect relevant persons from risks to them in case of fire. This will be determined by the findings of your risk assessment including the preventative measures you have or will have taken. In practice, it is very unlikely, that a properly conducted fire risk assessment, which takes into account all the matters relevant for the safety of persons in case of fire, will conclude that no fire precautions (including maintenance) are necessary.

sentences: Glossary entry 'Access room': A room through which the only escape route from an inner room passes.
Glossary entry 'Accommodation stairway': A stairway, additional to that required for means of escape purposes provided for the convenience of occupants.

Glossary entry 'Alterations notice': If your premises are considered by the enforcing authority to be high risk, they may issue an alterations notice that requires you to inform them before making any material alterations to your premises.

Glossary entry 'Alternative escape route': Escape routes sufficiently separated by either direction and space, or by fire-resisting construction to ensure that one is still available irrespective of the location of a fire.
Glossary entry 'Approved Document B (ADB)24': Guidance issued by Government in support of the fire safety aspects of the building regulations.

Glossary entry 'As low as reasonably practicable': A concept where risks should continue to be reduced until you reach a point where the cost and effort to reduce the risk further would be grossly disproportionate to the benefit achieved.
Glossary entry 'Automatic fire detection system': A means of automatically detecting the products of a fire and sending a signal to a fire warning system. See ‘Fire warning’.

Glossary entry 'Basement': A storey with a floor which at some point is more than 1,200mm below the highest level of ground adjacent to the outside walls, unless, and for escape purposes only, such area has adequate, independent and separate means of escape.
Glossary entry 'Child': Anyone who is not over compulsory school age, i.e. before or just after their 16th birthday.

Glossary entry 'Class 0, 1 or 3 surface spread of flame': Classes of surface spread of flame for materials needed to line the walls and ceilings of escape routes. See Appendix B for further information.
Glossary entry 'Combustible material': A substance that can be burned.
Glossary entry 'Compartment wall and/or floor': A fire-resisting wall or floor that separates one fire compartment from another.

Glossary entry 'Competent person': A person with enough training and experience or knowledge and other qualities to enable them properly to assist in undertaking the preventive and protective measures.

rows: A transparent panel in a wall or door of an inner room enabling the occupant to become aware of a fire in the access area during the early stages.

Low mounted luminous tracks positioned on escape routes in combination with exit indicators, exit marking and intermediate direction indicators along the route, provided for use when the supply to the normal lighting fails, which do not rely on an electrical supply for their luminous output.

The Order requires that fire precautions (such as firefighting equipment, fire detection and warning, and emergency routes and exits) should be provided (and maintained) ‘where necessary’. What this means is that the fire precautions you must provide (and maintain) are those which are needed to reasonably protect relevant persons from risks to them in case of fire. This will be determined by the findings of your risk assessment including the preventative measures you have or will have taken. In practice, it is very unlikely, that a properly conducted fire risk assessment, which takes into account all the matters relevant for the safety of persons in case of fire, will conclude that no fire precautions (including maintenance) are necessary.

(a) A person aged 16 years, from the date on which he attains that age until and including the 31st August which next follows that date. (b) A person aged 16 years and over who is undertaking a course of full-time education at a school or college which is not advanced education. (c) A person aged 16 years and over who is undertaking approved training that is not provided through a contract of employment. For the purposes of paragraphs (b) and (c) the person: (a) shall have commenced the course of full-time education or approved training before attaining the age of 19 years; and (b) shall not have attained the age of 20 years.

Glossary: Accommodation stairway means a stairway, additional to that required for means of escape purposes, provided for the convenience of occupants.

Glossary: Alterations notice means if your premises are considered by the enforcing authority to be high risk, they may issue an alterations notice that requires you to inform them before making any material alterations to your premises.

Glossary: Alternative escape route means escape routes sufficiently separated either by direction and space or by fire-resisting construction to ensure that one is still available irrespective of the location of a fire.
Glossary: Approved Document B (ADB)⁴⁶ means guidance issued by Government in support of the fire safety aspects of the building regulations.

rows: A transparent panel in a wall or door of an inner room enabling the occupant to become aware of a fire in the access area during the early stages.

Low mounted luminous tracks positioned on escape routes in combination with exit indicators, exit marking and intermediate direction indicators along the route, provided for use when the supply to the normal lighting fails, and which do not rely on an electrical supply for their luminous output.

The Order requires that fire precautions (such as firefighting equipment, fire detection and warning, and emergency routes and exits) should be provided (and maintained) ‘where necessary’. What this means is that the fire precautions you must provide (and maintain) are those which are needed to reasonably protect relevant persons from risks to them in case of fire. This will be determined by the findings of your risk assessment, including the preventative measures you have or will have taken. In practice, it is very unlikely that a properly conducted fire risk assessment, which takes into account all the matters relevant for the safety of persons in case of fire, will conclude that no fire precautions (including maintenance) are necessary.

(a) A person aged 16 years, from the date on which he attains that age until and including the 31 August which next follows that date. (b) A person aged 16 years and over who is undertaking a course of full-time education at a school or college which is not advanced education. (c) A person aged 16 years and over who is undertaking approved training that is not provided through a contract of employment. For the purposes of paragraphs (b) and (c), the person: (a) shall have commenced the course of full-time education or approved training before attaining the age of 19 years; and (b) shall not have attained the age of 20 years.

In the Glossary, Young person means (a) a person aged 16 years, from the date on which he attains that age until and including the 31 August which next follows that date; (b) a person aged 16 years and over who is undertaking a course of full-time education at a school or college which is not advanced education; or (c) a person aged 16 years and over who is undertaking approved training that is not provided through a contract of employment; for the purposes of paragraphs (b) and (c), the person (a) shall have commenced the course of full-time education or approved training before attaining the age of 19 years; and (b) shall not have attained the age of 20 years.

rows: The ability of a component or construction of a building to satisfy, for a stated period of time, some or all of the appropriate criteria of BS EN 1363-1, BS 476-7 and associated standards. (Generally described as 30 minutes fire-resisting or 60 minutes fire-resisting.)
A nominated person with responsibility for carrying out day-to-day management of fire safety. (This may or may not be the same as the ‘responsible person’.)
A number of planned and co-ordinated arrangements designed to reduce the risk of fire and to ensure safety of people in the event of fire.
A seal provided to close an imperfection of fit or design tolerance between elements or components, to restrict the passage of fire and smoke.
A means of alerting people to the existence of a fire. (See automatic fire detection system.)
Generally liquids with a flashpoint of below 21°C. (The Chemicals (Hazard Information and Packaging for Supply) Regulations 2002 (CHIP) give more detailed guidance.)
A room from which escape is possible only by passing through another room (the access room).
Any premises that require a licence under any statute to undertake trade or conduct business activities.
Emergency lighting that is kept illuminated at all relevant times.
An alteration to a building, process or service which significantly affects the level of risk in that building.
Route(s) provided to ensure safe egress from premises or other locations to a place of total safety, including the release of both personnel and animals from the buildings.
An organisation which accepts alarm signals from premises and carries out a pre-determined response.
Emergency lighting that illuminates only on failure of the normal supply.
A means of estimating the occupant capacity of a particular room or space in a building, based on an assumption of a certain number of m² for each person.
The physiological and psychological characteristics of the individuals who may reasonably be expected to use the building.
A system of evacuation in which different parts of the premises are evacuated in a controlled sequence of phases, those parts of the premises expected to be at greatest risk being evacuated first.
A place, away from the building, in which people are at no immediate danger from the effects of a fire.

Glossary of terms, Fire safety manager: A nominated person with responsibility for carrying out day-to-day management of fire safety. (This may or may not be the same as the ‘responsible person’.)
Glossary of terms, Fire safety strategy: A number of planned and co-ordinated arrangements designed to reduce the risk of fire and to ensure safety of people in the event of fire.
Glossary of terms, Fire-stopping: A seal provided to close an imperfection of fit or design tolerance between elements or components, to restrict the passage of fire and smoke.
Glossary of terms, Fire warning system: A means of alerting people to the existence of a fire. (See automatic fire detection system.)

Glossary of terms, Highly flammable: Generally liquids with a flashpoint of below 21°C. (The Chemicals (Hazard Information and Packaging for Supply) Regulations 2002 (CHIP) give more detailed guidance.)
Glossary of terms, Inner room: A room from which escape is possible only by passing through another room (the access room).
Glossary of terms, Licensed premises: Any premises that require a licence under any statute to undertake trade or conduct business activities.
Glossary of terms, Maintained lighting: Emergency lighting that is kept illuminated at all relevant times.
Glossary of terms, Material change: An alteration to a building, process or service which significantly affects the level of risk in that building.

Glossary of terms, Means of escape: Route(s) provided to ensure safe egress from premises or other locations to a place of total safety, including the release of both personnel and animals from the buildings.
Glossary of terms, Monitoring station: An organisation which accepts alarm signals from premises and carries out a pre-determined response.
Glossary of terms, Non-maintained lighting: Emergency lighting that illuminates only on failure of the normal supply.
Glossary of terms, Occupancy density factor: A means of estimating the occupant capacity of a particular room or space in a building, based on an assumption of a certain number of m² for each person.
Glossary of terms, Occupancy profile: The physiological and psychological characteristics of the individuals who may reasonably be expected to use the building.

Glossary of terms, Phased evacuation: A system of evacuation in which different parts of the premises are evacuated in a controlled sequence of phases, those parts of the premises expected to be at greatest risk being evacuated first.
Glossary of terms, Place of total safety: A place, away from the building, in which people are at no immediate danger from the effects of a fire.

sentences: Glossary, Access room: A room through which the only escape route from an inner room passes.
Glossary, Accommodation stairway: A stairway, additional to that required for means of escape purposes, provided for the convenience of occupants.

Glossary, Alterations notice: If your premises are considered by the enforcing authority to be high risk, they may issue an alterations notice that requires you to inform them before making any material alterations to your premises.

Glossary, Alternative escape route: Escape routes sufficiently separated by either direction and space, or by fire-resisting construction to ensure that one is still available irrespective of the location of a fire.
Glossary, Approved Document B (ADB): Guidance issued by Government in support of the fire safety aspects of the building regulations.

Glossary, Basement: A storey with a floor which at some point is more than 1,200mm below the highest level of ground adjacent to the outside walls, unless, and for escape purposes only, such area has adequate, independent and separate means of escape.

Glossary, Combustible material: A substance that can be burned.
Glossary, Compartment wall and/or floor: A fire-resisting wall or floor that separates one fire compartment from another.

rows: A transparent panel in a wall or door of an inner room enabling the occupant to become aware of a fire in the access area during the early stages.

Low mounted luminous tracks positioned on escape routes in combination with exit indicators, exit marking and intermediate direction indicators along the route, provided for use when the supply to the normal lighting fails, which do not rely on an electrical supply for their luminous output

The Order requires that fire precautions (such as firefighting equipment, fire detection and warning, and emergency routes and exits) should be provided (and maintained) ‘where necessary’. What this means is that the fire precautions you must provide (and maintain) are those which are needed to reasonably protect relevant persons from risks to them in case of fire. This will be determined by the findings of your risk assessment, including the preventative measures you have or will have taken. In practice, it is very unlikely that a properly conducted fire risk assessment, which takes into account all the matters relevant for the safety of persons in case of fire, will conclude that no fire precautions (including maintenance) are necessary.

(a) A person aged 16 years, from the date on which he attains that age until and including the 31st August which next follows that date. (b) A person aged 16 years and over who is undertaking a course of full-time education at a school or college which is not advanced education. (c) A person aged 16 years and over who is undertaking approved training that is not provided through a contract of employment. For the purposes of paragraphs (b) and (c) the person: (a) shall have commenced the course of full-time education or approved training before attaining the age of 19 years; and (b) shall not have attained the age of 20 years.

Glossary: Young person means (a) a person aged 16 years, from the date on which he attains that age until and including the 31st August which next follows that date; (b) a person aged 16 years and over who is undertaking a course of full-time education at a school or college which is not advanced education; or (c) a person aged 16 years and over who is undertaking approved training that is not provided through a contract of employment, where for paragraphs (b) and (c) the person shall have commenced the course of full-time education or approved training before attaining the age of 19 years and shall not have attained the age of 20 years.

Glossary: Dead end – Area from which escape is possible in one direction only.

sentences: Glossary: Fire compartment – A building, or part of a building, constructed to prevent the spread of fire to or from another part of the same building or an adjoining building.

Glossary: Fire door – A door or shutter, together with its frame and furniture, provided for the passage of people, air or goods which, when closed, is intended to restrict the passage of fire and/or smoke to a predictable level of performance.
Glossary: Firefighting lift – A lift, designed to have additional protection, with controls that enable it to be used under the direct control of the fire and rescue service when fighting a fire.
Glossary: Firefighting shaft – A fire-resisting enclosure containing a firefighting stair, fire mains, firefighting lobbies and, if provided, a firefighting lift.
Glossary: Firefighting stairway – See firefighting shaft.

Glossary: Fire resistance – The ability of a component or construction of a building to satisfy, for a stated period of time, some or all of the appropriate criteria of relevant standards. (Generally described as 30 minutes fire-resisting or 60 minutes fire-resisting.) See BS EN 1363-1, BS 476-7 and associated standards for further information.
Glossary: Fire safety manager – A nominated person with responsibility for carrying out day-to-day management of fire safety. (This may or may not be the same as the ‘responsible person’.).
Glossary: Fire safety strategy – A number of planned and co-ordinated arrangements designed to reduce the risk of fire and to ensure the safety of people if there is a fire.
Glossary: Fire stopping – A seal provided to close an imperfection of fit or design tolerance between elements or components, to restrict the passage of fire and smoke.
Glossary: Fire-warning system – A means of alerting people to the existence of a fire. (See automatic fire-detection system.).
Glossary: Flammable material – Easily ignited and capable of burning rapidly.
Glossary: Hazardous substances – 1. See Dangerous substance. 2. A substance subject to the Control of Substances Hazardous to Health Regulations 2002 (COSHH).
Glossary: Healthcare premises – A hospital treatment centre, health centre, clinic, surgery, walk-in centre or other premises where patiets are provided with medical care by a clinician.
Glossary: Highly flammable – Generally liquids with a flashpoint of below 21°C. (The Chemicals Hazard Information and Packaging for Supply Regulations 2002 (CHIP) give more detailed guidance.).

Glossary: sub-compartment wall and/or floor means a fire-resisting wall or floor that further separates spaces within a fire compartment from another, typically used to provide temporary refuge during progressive horizontal evacuation of patients within the compartment of fire origin.

Glossary: Dead end means: area from which escape is possible in one direction only.

Glossary: Fire safety manager means: a nominated person with responsibility for carrying out day-to-day management of fire safety. (This may or may not be the same as the ‘responsible person’.).

rows: 1. A substance which because of its physico-chemical or chemical properties and the way it is used or is present at the workplace creates a risk. 2. A substance subject to the Dangerous Substance and Explosive Atmosphere Regulations 2002 (DSEAR).
Area from which escape is possible in one direction only.
The shortest distance from any point within the floor area to the nearest storey exit, or fire-resisting route, ignoring walls, partitions and fixings.
Premises occupied as a private dwelling, excluding those areas used in common by the occupants of more than one such dwelling.
Lighting provided to illuminate escape routes that will function if the normal lighting fails.

Route forming that part of the means of escape from any point in a building to a final exit.
A lift that may be used for the evacuation of people with disabilities, or others, in a fire.

A fire signal, usually from a fire warning system, resulting from a cause other than fire.
An exit from a building where people can continue to disperse in safety and where they are no longer at danger from fire and/or smoke.
A building, or part of a building, constructed to prevent the spread of fire to or from another part of the same building or an adjoining building.

A door or shutter, together with its frame and furniture, provided for the passage of people, air or goods which, when closed is intended to restrict the passage of fire and/or smoke to a predictable level of performance.
A lift, designed to have additional protection, with controls that enable it to be used under the direct control of the fire and rescue service when fighting a fire.
A fire-resisting enclosure containing a firefighting stair, fire mains, firefighting lobbies and if provided, a firefighting lift.
sentences: Glossary: Dangerous substance: 1. A substance which because of its physico-chemical or chemical properties and the way it is used or is present at the workplace creates a risk. 2. A substance subject to the Dangerous Substance and Explosive Atmosphere Regulations 2002 (DSEAR).
Glossary: Dead end: Area from which escape is possible in one direction only.
Glossary: Direct distance: The shortest distance from any point within the floor area to the nearest storey exit, or fire-resisting route, ignoring walls, partitions and fixings.
Glossary: Domestic premises: Premises occupied as a private dwelling, excluding those areas used in common by the occupants of more than one such dwelling.
Glossary: Emergency escape lighting: Lighting provided to illuminate escape routes that will function if the normal lighting fails.
Glossary: Enforcing authority: The fire and rescue authority or any other authority specified in Article 25 of the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005.
Glossary: Escape route: Route forming that part of the means of escape from any point in a building to a final exit.
Glossary: Evacuation lift: A lift that may be used for the evacuation of people with disabilities, or others, in a fire.
Glossary: External escape stair: Stair providing an escape route, external to the building.
Glossary: Fail-safe: Locking an output device with the application of power and having the device unlock when the power is removed. Also known as fail unlock, reverse action or power locked.
Glossary: False alarm: A fire signal, usually from a fire warning system, resulting from a cause other than fire.
Glossary: Final exit: An exit from a building where people can continue to disperse in safety and where they are no longer at danger from fire and/or smoke.
Glossary: Fire compartment: A building, or part of a building, constructed to prevent the spread of fire to or from another part of the same building or an adjoining building.

Glossary: Fire door: A door or shutter, together with its frame and furniture, provided for the passage of people, air or goods which, when closed is intended to restrict the passage of fire and/or smoke to a predictable level of performance.
Glossary: Firefighting lift: A lift, designed to have additional protection, with controls that enable it to be used under the direct control of the fire and rescue service when fighting a fire.
Glossary: Firefighting shaft: A fire-resisting enclosure containing a firefighting stair, fire mains, firefighting lobbies and if provided, a firefighting lift.
Glossary: Firefighting stairway: See firefighting shaft.

rows: The ability of a component or construction of a building to satisfy, for a stated period of time, some or all of the appropriate criteria of relevant standards. (Generally described as 30 minutes fire-resisting or 60 minutes fire-resisting.) See BS EN 1363-1,⁴⁵ BS 476-7³² and associated standards for further information.
A nominated person with responsibility for carrying out day-to-day management of fire safety. (This may or may not be the same as the ‘responsible person’.)
A number of planned and co-ordinated arrangements designed to reduce the risk of fire and to ensure the safety of people if there is a fire.
A seal provided to close an imperfection of fit or design tolerance between elements or components, to restrict the passage of fire and smoke.
A means of alerting people to the existence of a fire. (See automatic fire detection system.)
Easily ignited and capable of burning rapidly.
Generally liquids with a flashpoint of below 21°C. (The Chemicals Hazard Information and Packaging for Supply Regulations 2002⁴⁶ (CHIP) give more detailed guidance.)
1. See Dangerous substance. 2. A substance subject to the Control of Substances Hazardous to Health Regulations 2002 (COSHH).
A room from which escape is possible only by passing through another room (the access room).
Any premises that require a licence under any statute to undertake trade or conduct business activities.
An alteration to the premises, process or service which significantly affects the level of risk to people from fire in those premises.
Route(s) provided to ensure safe egress from the premises or other locations to a place of total safety.
A system of evacuation in which different parts of the premises are evacuated in a controlled sequence of phases, those parts of the premises expected to be at greatest risk being evacuated first.

A place within a building or structure where, for a limited period of time, people will have some protection from the effects of fire and smoke. This place, usually a corridor or stairway, will normally have a minimum of 30 minutes fire resistance and allow people to continue their escape to a place of total safety.
A place, away from the building, in which people are at no immediate danger from the effects of a fire.
sentences: Glossary: Fire resistance: The ability of a component or construction of a building to satisfy, for a stated period of time, some or all of the appropriate criteria of relevant standards. (Generally described as 30 minutes fire-resisting or 60 minutes fire-resisting.) See BS EN 1363-1,⁴⁵ BS 476-7³² and associated standards for further information.
Glossary: Fire safety manager: A nominated person with responsibility for carrying out day-to-day management of fire safety. (This may or may not be the same as the ‘responsible person’.)
Glossary: Fire safety strategy: A number of planned and co-ordinated arrangements designed to reduce the risk of fire and to ensure the safety of people if there is a fire.
Glossary: Fire stopping: A seal provided to close an imperfection of fit or design tolerance between elements or components, to restrict the passage of fire and smoke.
Glossary: Fire-warning system: A means of alerting people to the existence of a fire. (See automatic fire detection system.)
Glossary: Flammable material: Easily ignited and capable of burning rapidly.
Glossary: Highly flammable: Generally liquids with a flashpoint of below 21°C. (The Chemicals Hazard Information and Packaging for Supply Regulations 2002⁴⁶ (CHIP) give more detailed guidance.)
Glossary: Hazardous substance: 1. See Dangerous substance. 2. A substance subject to the Control of Substances Hazardous to Health Regulations 2002 (COSHH).
Glossary: Inner room: A room from which escape is possible only by passing through another room (the access room).
Glossary: Licensed premises: Any premises that require a licence under any statute to undertake trade or conduct business activities.
Glossary: Material change: An alteration to the premises, process or service which significantly affects the level of risk to people from fire in those premises.
Glossary: Means of escape: Route(s) provided to ensure safe egress from the premises or other locations to a place of total safety.

Glossary: Phased evacuation: A system of evacuation in which different parts of the premises are evacuated in a controlled sequence of phases, those parts of the premises expected to be at greatest risk being evacuated first.

Glossary: Place of reasonable safety: A place within a building or structure where, for a limited period of time, people will have some protection from the effects of fire and smoke. This place, usually a corridor or stairway, will normally have a minimum of 30 minutes fire resistance and allow people to continue their escape to a place of total safety.
Glossary: Place of total safety: A place, away from the building, in which people are at no immediate danger from the effects of a fire.
